Key.Original: Linear-reservoir recession rate per day for groundwater baseflow. USGS SIR 2022-5114 gives 0.9 to 0.99 per day for a perennial stream, which is this value as a daily retention.
Key.English: Linear-reservoir recession rate per day for groundwater baseflow. USGS SIR 2022-5114 gives 0.9 to 0.99 per day for a perennial stream, which is this value as a daily retention.

Key.Original: Bed slope in metres per metre. Manning rating sets the stage from the discharge, and a steeper bed carries the same flow at a lower stage.
Key.English: Bed slope in metres per metre. Manning rating sets the stage from the discharge, and a steeper bed carries the same flow at a lower stage.

Key.Original: Area in square metres draining to the river point. A river stage responds to everything upstream, so this is the contributing area rather than the routing cell. 250000 is a small stream catchment.
Key.English: Area in square metres draining to the river point. A river stage responds to everything upstream, so this is the contributing area rather than the routing cell. 250000 is a small stream catchment.

Key.Original: Log hydrology diagnostics to the RPT. Turn this on before reporting a fault.
Key.English: Log hydrology diagnostics to the RPT. Turn this on before reporting a fault.

Key.Original: Manning roughness coefficient n for the channel. 0.030 to 0.050 is a natural stream (Chow 1959); 0.025 is smooth earth.
Key.English: Manning roughness coefficient n for the channel. 0.030 to 0.050 is a natural stream (Chow 1959); 0.025 is smooth earth.

Key.Original: Nash-cascade storage coefficient per 5 s tick; 1/k = reservoir time constant
Key.English: Nash-cascade storage coefficient per 5 s tick; 1/k = reservoir time constant

Key.Original: Width in metres of the modelled river section. Rising runoff is spread over a 100 m catchment cell and divided by this width to give the water-level rise.
Key.English: Width in metres of the modelled river section. Rising runoff is spread over a 100 m catchment cell and divided by this width to give the water-level rise.

Key.Original: Distance in metres inland that the tide raises the river level. Full tidal amplitude at the coast, falling to zero at this distance.
Key.English: Distance in metres inland that the tide raises the river level. Full tidal amplitude at the coast, falling to zero at this distance.
